articles.title: Why rising Treasury yields are becoming a growing risk for the US economy
articles.excerpt:
A sell-off in U.S. Treasuries has pushed yields higher, raising borrowing costs for households, companies and the federal government. Higher yields could pressure mortgages, corporate investment, asset valuations and government debt servicing. Investors are watching inflation, energy risks, Federal Reserve policy, Treasury supply and foreign demand for signs of prolonged market pressure.

articles.title: IDFC First Bank raises $500 million via maiden international bond issuance
articles.excerpt:
This is the bank’s first international bond issuance and marks its entry into the global debt capital markets. | Photo Credit: Gerra Madhusudan 10751@Chennai

IDFC First Bank on Wednesday said it has raised $500 million in debt, with global investors like BlackRock, Capital Group, and Alliancebernstein anchoring its maiden international bond issuance.

The bank, through its IFSC Banking Unit at GIFT City, issued the bonds having a tenure of three years and a fixed coupon of 5.625 per cent.

The notes were placed with investors outside the US in Regulation S format, IDFC First Bank said in a statement.

articles.title: Selloff in euro zone bonds pauses but oil prices keep up pressure
articles.excerpt:

However, the ongoing surge in oil prices maintained upward pressure on markets. Concerns about inflation and borrowing led to notable selling in longer-dated bonds, with France's 30-year yield experiencing a remarkable increase, especially during the budget season and electoral period.

articles.title: Euro zone bonds join global selloff, long-end yields at multi-year highs
articles.excerpt:
On Tuesday, yields on longer-dated euro zone bonds surged to levels not seen in years. The increasing oil prices, spurred by diminishing expectations for a quick resolution to the conflict in Iran, intensified inflation worries throughout the markets. Consequently, investors are anticipating a quarter-point interest rate hike from the ECB, while apprehensions about fiscal stability in various nations add pressure on global bonds.
